javaOop.title: Java OOP & Dynamic Method Dispatch (vtable)
javaOop.subtitle: Master Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and how the JVM resolves virtual methods using the vtable.
javaOop.mentalModel: Polymorphism lets a superclass reference point to any subclass instance. At runtime, the JVM uses the invokevirtual opcode to inspect the instance's virtual method table (vtable) in Metaspace and jump to the correct overridden method implementation.

failureModes: ClassCastException vs AbstractMethodError: ClassCastException occurs when attempting to downcast an object reference to an incompatible subclass type. AbstractMethodError occurs at runtime if a class compiled against an abstract method interface is run without providing an implementation.
tradeOffs: Virtual Method Dispatch vs Direct Inline Calls: Virtual methods require a vtable memory lookup at runtime. Non-overridable methods (private, final, static) use invokestatic/invokespecial, allowing the JVM JIT compiler to inline the call directly into native code.
theoryData.productionScenario: A payment gateway plugin architecture used polymorphism with `PaymentProcessor` interfaces. During a high-concurrency event, the JVM JIT compiler applied Monomorphic Call Site Optimization on `processor.pay()`, inlining `StripeProcessor.pay()` directly into native assembly and eliminating vtable lookup overhead.

interviewQA.q: How does the JVM execute polymorphic method calls at runtime?
interviewQA.a: The JVM bytecode instruction `invokevirtual` reads the object's class metadata pointer in the object header on the Heap, navigates to the class's Virtual Method Table (`vtable`) in Metaspace, and jumps to the exact method address stored at that slot index.

quizData.question: Can `static` or `private` methods be overridden in Java subclasses?
quizData.answer: NO! `static` methods belong to the class and are resolved at compile-time (`invokestatic`). `private` methods are hidden from subclasses (`invokespecial`). Neither uses the `vtable`.

quizData.question: What is the key difference between Method Overloading and Method Overriding?
quizData.answer: Overloading occurs within the SAME class with different parameter signatures resolved at COMPILE-TIME. Overriding occurs across SUBCLASSES with identical method signatures resolved at RUNTIME via the vtable.
